# The Scaleflayer Menagerie

*Pages PDF 99-104*

## **The Scaleflayer Menagerie**
## **Unleash the Beasts of War**
Elves have a strong affinity with the natural world, their armies often accompanied by wondrous creatures of land, sea, and sky. For the elves of Ulthuan or those of the Old World’s forests, such companions are earned through trust, built upon empathy, respect, or a mutual enemy. The dark elves of Naggaroth take this connection and twist it to their own survival. Few dark elf forces make war without the support of terrifying beasts of war, and so a warren of tunnels filled with deadly and curious monsters lies within _Temple of Spite’s_ bedrock. These are watched over by the beastmasters of Clar Karond, arguably the most accomplished of their kind. 

_Temple of Spite_ ’s beastmasters are an insular group, even among the fractured society of a black ark. They must protect their own lives and those of the mounts and war beasts they command, as essential to Helbane’s martial ambitions. There are few foes who can stand against the charge of the dark elves’ cold one cavalry or survive long against a trained war hydra. More terrifying still are the fleet’s sea monsters, over whom only the beastmasters can exercise effective control. 

Few amongst _Temple of Spite_ ’s inhabitants show the beastmasters due respect. To many highborn, the beastmasters are another form of skilled servant, who understand little beyond the beasts they tend. Such thinking drives the beastmasters further from the company of other dark elves. 

## **Goals**
0 **Keep their beasts.** The menagerie is composed mainly of beasts of war or burden, and it is the responsibility of the beastmasters to tend to them.The beasts must be ready for battle, for a highborn to ride, or to pull a seagoing vessel. 

- **Represent Clar Karond’s beastmasters.** As the black ark’s Lord of Beasts, Scorath is charged by his masters in the city to enhance the reputation of the beastmasters. 

- **Discover and catalogue exotic beasts.** The beastmasters have an appetite for discovery. 

- **Maintain the captives.** Forced labour is essential in the running of _Temple of Spite_ , and this responsibility is vital. 

## **Internal Tensions**
## **Contest of Claws**
The cities of clar Karond and Karond Kar both make claims to naggaroth’s most accomplished beastmasters, a rivalry they settle once a year at the contest of claws. here, beastmasters stake both their own lives and those of their charges in elaborate formal battles, the winner earning the fleeting glory of their city and a much-enhanced reputation. The contest is always close, with a flurry of assassinations and accidents marking the days before it. 

Scaleflayer and his beastmasters hope to dominate the contest this year with their prized pets, but Karond Kar is already attempting sabotage. Their agents have inveigled their way into the ranks of _Temple of Spite’_ s captives and even the beastmasters’ own ranks. These infiltrators seek every opportunity to kill or injure their rivals, but even greater glory awaits anyone who can steal creatures for their own masters’ collection. 

The beastmasters are not free from internal discord, as Scaleflayer’s abrasive leadership breeds resentment, especially amongst the whelpmasters, whom he treats with the same disdain with which the highborn treat him. These lower beastmasters hope to rise in the hierarchy to tame more impressive beasts than wretched captives or slavering hounds, and being resentful, they have a habit of sabotaging each other to elevate their reputation. 

Beastmasters are also notoriously territorial: they consider their pens and charges solely their own responsibility, and should any other attempt to encroach, they may challenge them to a duel. For example, Lithen Ashbane is especially ambitious, eager to pass on her kharibdyss to tame greater sea monsters, which are the current preserve of Terynth Nathkin. 

## **In the Old World**
## **On the Black Ark**
The beastmasters are numerous, though it is rare for them to gather in full and they do not appear in force. Most keep to their stations, looking after their beasts without sparing attention for intrigue. Others are further afield, assigned to ships or sea monsters in the fleet. It is rare to meet more than two or three full-ranked beastmasters at a time, the typical number assigned to each pen or stable. Below them are the whelpmasters, lowranked beastmasters left in charge of the black ark’s captives or hunting hounds. Each is a petty tyrant, jealously guarding their power. 

## **Rivals and Allies**
Aboard _Temple of Spite_ , the beastmasters have few allies. Captain Manbane may be their strongest advocate, as his enthusiasm for harnessing beasts for ships brings him close to the high beastmaster. The followers of Khaine have some appreciation of the beastmasters, for they provide them with captives to slay during their gory rites. 

Meanwhile, many on the Black Convocation grow tired of Scaleflayer’s prickly disposition. Supreme Sorceress and her coven would rather see Kelrathi rise to high beastmaster. The second-in-command is seen as far more pliable and open to providing ritual sacrifices and spell ingredients made from body parts. Only the political importance of Clar Karond’s beastmasters prevent the sorceresses from making a move. Anethra Helbane does not want to upset the delicate political balance in the ark’s home city. 

Scorath and his followers continue their hunt for new and stranger creatures to add to their menagerie. They have cultivated local guides and informers along the western coastline of Bretonnia, the northern coast of the Empire and openly amongst the Bjornling and Skaeling Norse. In more civilised lands, they are discrete and dress as wood elves. Most of their contacts believe their elf liaison is nothing more than an eccentric elven collector. 

These unwitting spies are told to send word back to Scaleflayer via the raiding fleet or the Glass Thorn. If _Temple of Spite_ ventures close in good time, the beastmasters ride out in small groups. Two or three beastmasters lead a scouting band in scourgerunner chariots to hunt down their prey. These bands are accompanied by captives hauling cages and chained nets, or bound and drugged to act as bait. Should anyone happen across them, they may well find themselves in those cages. One way or another, the beastmasters of Clar Karond ensure that they never return empty-handed. 

## **Meeting the Beastmasters**
Clearly, the Characters would make fine captives or fodder for the beasts, but the beastmasters may have another role for them first. Finding and capturing new creatures is a challenge, and local expertise, disposable scouts, and tasty bait are all part of a successful hunter’s strategy. These are all roles that the Characters can fulfil. 

On the ark, Scaleflayer’s dislike of politics leaves him open to those who might get involved in intrigue on his behalf. If the Characters have powerful patrons already, the high beastmaster would tolerate them acting in his interests, such as making landfall where new creatures might be found, or punishing a particularly obnoxious highborn. 

## **Disposition**
Scaleflayer’s full command includes beastmasters, their charges, and lowborn servants: 

- **High Beastmaster Scorath Scaleflayer** represents the beastmasters on the Black Convocation and directs their efforts in raids and warfare. He tires of politics and will take to the field atop his scourgerunner chariot (driven by his dedicated charioteer and daughter, Tiratha) to hunt down new creatures. 

- **Beastmaster Kelrathi** is Scaleflayer’s second-incommand and overseer of the breeding plans and research endeavours. She rarely takes to the field, preferring her workshop and dissection rooms, but has been known to ride and drive a pack of three cold ones with almost preternatural command. 

- There are 23 individual Beastmasters under Scaleflayer’s command, each an individual with their own beasts to tend and ambitions. 

## **Look Fair and Feel Foal — Easy Encounter**
Characters encounter some of _Temple of Spite’s_ beastmasters as they hunt new beasts in the coastal highlands somewhere in the Old World. Beastmaster Rylveth does not want a fight, so they present themselves as high elves. 

Make an **Opposed Perception** Test between the Characters and the dark rider to see which group first notices the other. Should the dark elves win, they gain +1 SL on any Tests made to lie as they prepare their disguises. 

The dark elves ask for help in capturing a hippogryph foal. They offer 15 GC, with an additional 30 GC if they capture the mother too. The dark elves lead them to the nest, directing them to draw the mother’s attention while they capture the foal. 

If the Characters realise they are Druchii, Rylveth negotiates, claiming that elves are all alike and they present no threat. They only fight if forced to, preferring to make an escape by sacrificing the hounds to divert the Characters’ attention. If the dark elves have numeric advantage, they try to capture the Characters. 

This encounter is an opportunity to learn more of the dark elves and potentially even the ark. In their arrogance, Rylveth and the corsairs are relatively open with the Characters and the beastmaster opines on his philosophy on life and other species, veiled behind pronouncements on ‘how one should treat beasts’. 

   - 1 Dark Elf Beastmaster with a net and a sword 

- 29 whelpmasters are apprenticed to the beastmasters, overseeing captives and warhounds under supervision of their superiors. 

- A band of 3 Dark Elves on Dark Steeds act as Scouts and trackers. 

- 3 hunting hounds — use the Dog profile add Traits: _Size (Average)_ , _Tracker_ , _Trained (Broken, Guard, War)_ 

- 3 Dark Elf Corsairs with a sword, a repeater handbow, and a net each 

- 1 Dark Rider armed with a spear and net 

## **Deadliest Game — Medium Encounter**

- Bands of captives, between 30-45 at any time, do the most dangerous jobs for Scorath. 

- The menagerie has a shifting population of creatures, as new charges are found and others die. 

## **Appearance**
Most beastmasters go lightly armoured to better dodge snapping jaws and swiping claws. Many decorate themselves with tanned hides or talismans made from the creatures they command, signalling their respective status to their fellow beastmasters. 

Beastmaster Kelrathi wishes to test a surgically altered hydra hatchling. By night, she brings the creature to the outskirts of a settlement, just as the Characters pass by. 

Kelrathi’s experiments have robbed the hydra of its regenerative powers, though it now has the _Corrosive Blood_ Trait. The hydra itself is not immune to the effects and suffers an additional wound each time it is injured. The hydra is stealthy and uses darkness to its advantage. As a hatchling, it cannot breathe fire. 

Three groups of dark elves follow the hydra’s progress. They are composed of three dreadspears each, led by a beastmaster, with the third led by Kelrathi. The warriors use their spears to drive the hydra forwards. If the hydra risks dying, two groups rush the Characters while Kelrathi directs the hydra to safety. 

Kelrathi’s expedition consists of: 

## **The Black Council**

- 1 Hydra with the _Corrosive Blood_ and _Stealthy_ Traits, but without the _Breath (Fire)_ or _Regenerate_ Traits 

- Kelrathi, accompanied by 3 Dark Elf Warriors with spears and shields, ten yards behind the hydra 

- Two groups, each composed of 1 Beastmaster accompanied by 3 Dark Elf Warriors with spears, ten yards from the hydra’s left or right flank 

## **Breaking Some Eggs — Hard Encounter**
Scorath Scaleflayer has heard a sea dragon is nesting in a cave very close to a human settlement. He covets its eggs but there is no way to secure them without alerting the villagers and garrison. Duriath Helbane refuses to waste resources on scouring the settlement, so the high beastmaster must distract the humans with an attack while he descends to the sea dragon’s lair. The beastmasters plan a clifftop assault on the village stockade, sending monsters to keep the humans busy. The Characters are in this large village, or close enough to see events unfolding. 

The beastmasters and their monsters line up outside the village. The defenders focus their efforts on the weaker points in the defences, where the Characters have their best chance at defending the settlement alongside the garrison. Meanwhile, Scorath and two beastmasters abseil down to the cave. Stealthy or athletic Characters may row or climb after them while the village fights off the attack. 

The sea dragon sleeps inside the cave, its body wrapped around its eggs. If undisturbed, it will sleep for another decade. It can be woken eif it suffers a Wound or if any of its eggs are damaged. The sea dragon chases down any creature it sees and will not stop until everything is dead. If the eggs are stolen, it attacks the village. 

The beastmaster war party is comprised of: 

- High Beastmaster Scorath Scaleflayer accompanied by Beastmaster Kelrathi and 4 Dark Elf Corsairs with 2 swords and a repeater handbow each 

- A Beastmaster driving on eight unridden Cold Ones from a Scourgerunner chariot, assaulting the western walls 

- A Beastmaster driving on a War Hydra, assaulting the eastern walls 

- A Beastmaster driving on a Kharibdyss, assaulting the northern gate 

Malerion’s inner circle is made up of exactly one hundred lords and ladies of naggaroth, though not all are living. claiming a seat at the obsidian table is one of the highest honours, but also one of the most dangerous. The Dread King is nothing if not mercurial in his favours, and it is not unusual for fewer dreadlords to leave the chamber than entered it. 

Down the ages, there have always been nobles clever enough to avoid falling to the Dread King’s explosive temper, and it is no different now. closest of all Malerion’s councillors is his mother, Morathi. This honour is not granted out of filial regard, but because the hag Sorceress can be trusted only when kept in plain sight. Kouran, captain of the Black guard, is a different matter entirely, for his loyalty to the Dread King is without question. The third most influential seat on the council belongs to the cadaverous noble known only as ezresor, a particularly cold-blooded individual widely assumed to be Malerion’s spymaster, though this has never been officially confirmed. 

Venil chillblade, latest incumbent of a seat that has become almost a hereditary privilege, holds sway over fleets that plough the seas east of naggaroth, whilst the darkly beautiful Drane Brackblood directs the plunder of the westward realms. command of naggaroth’s armies is split between several nobles, of whom the heavily scarred Ebnir Soulflayer is most prominent. his is perhaps the most tenuous seat on the council, for he earns glory for every victory and blame for every defeat. So far, Soulflayer has managed to shift any blame to other, now dead, council members, but this game can only be played for so long. 

## **Showdown with Triton**
lord Skaris is castellan of the Vanguard Spires and obsessed with Triton, the ocean-dwelling demigod with a special loathing for dark elves. a seer told Skaris that his fate is to die impaled on Triton’s trident and he is taking steps to prevent this happening. he has acquired a scroll to summon Triton and intends to deploy the might of _Temple of Spite_ to destroy him once and for all. Several reaver captains and sorceresses have seen Triton’s rage against the Druchii and pledged to help. Skaris has one problem: no dark elf can compel Triton to appear. he needs someone from another species to read the scroll. 

- A flock of 10 Harpies to attack people in the streets 

## **High Beastmaster Scorath Scaleflayer**
A quiet, thoughtful elf, Scorath’s scars bear testament to his journey becoming _Temple of Spite_ ’s High Beastmaster. He began life as a street urchin in Clar Karond, but escaped this fate through his innate connection with beasts. Word spread of his underground pit fights, with mongrels, giant rats, and worse dying at his command. This earned him a place among the beastmasters, where his talent saw a swift ascent.

## **The Creature Parade**
During the Season of Savagery, the high Beastmaster leads a procession around the ark, where the beastmasters goad many of their beasts on deck for all to see. It is a fine display of scales, fur, and feathers and an unsubtle reminder of the beastmasters’ power on board. This year, Teryn nathkin and several other beastmasters are curious to see what happens if a hydra gets loose for a few minutes. Who will it attack first? If Scorath discovered the plan, he would suppress it. he knows the Black Convocation would enjoy the bloodshed, then blame the beastmasters. 

## **Beastmaster Kelrathi**

Kelrathi is an oddity among beastmasters, more often found with a quill than a lash, yet no one can match her when it comes to knowledge of beasts, their care, or their anatomy. Kelrathi serves as the black ark’s pre-eminent beast healer and Scorath’s second-in-command — perfect for him as she holds no political ambition. After all, to rise to high beastmaster would take Kelrathi away from her precious studies. She is fascinated by the creatures in her care, many of which are twisted by magic, which she combines with surgery and selective breeding to enhance their biology. Unlike most on the black ark, she sees no reason why her art should not be applied to elves. 

**Scalpel** (52/+5) 

**Bite** (45/+6) Lose Advantage to make this free attack 

**Armour Toughness Bonus:** 3 **Scales:** +3 AP **Skills** 

Animal Care 78, Animal Training 72, Channelling ( _Ghur_ ) 68, Charm Animal 70, Cool 80, Evaluate 72, Heal 78, Language (Magick 70, Reikspiel 82), Lore (Beasts 96, Chemistry 76, Medicine 77), Melee (Basic) 52, Perception 67, Research 72, Trade (Apothecary 70, Poisoner 70) 

Kelrathi does not believe Druchii superior in all ways; to her, there is room for improvement. To this end, Kelrathi performs endless experiments, dissections, and spellcraft. She has cultivated strong connections with the black ark’s sorceresses, offering them choice sacrifices and poisonous concoctions in return for tutelage. Rumour has it the beastmaster has even experimented upon herself, sporting scales beneath her robes. Few would dare suggest such a thing in Kelrathi’s presence, for to underestimate Kelrathi risks becoming her next test subject.

## **Meeting Moulder**
Clan Moulder are skaven who shape flesh and breed monsters in service of the Under-empire. The Druchii see their methods as crude and inelegant, but they can’t deny the effectiveness of their experiments. Kelrathi wants to broker a meeting with a master moulder to compare techniques and theories. The characters could be sent with beastmaster oversight to seek skaven contacts on her behalf. Or they might encounter a skaven patrol accompanied by Kelrathi on their way to a rendezvous with a master moulder somewhere in the Old World.
